mobbin:f4a1c6f0-b7ae-427b-a896-b4f3c2535.summary: From For you the user taps TV Nearby and picks Living Room TV from a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth discovery list. They confirm selection, see Turning on, then a persistent Connected bar with a remote shortcut.
steps: For you screen with TV Nearby round button
Select a device: Living Room TV list
Select a device: Living Room TV checked
Short message: Turning on Living Room TV
Connected bar: Living Room TV and remote
steal: Named devices under AVAILABLE DEVICES (screen 2) show room or screen identity before control.
A green check on the selected TV (screen 3) confirms which screen before committing.
A Turning on message then Connected with the named TV (screens 4 to 5) gives power and link feedback.
A persistent Connected bar with a remote shortcut (screen 5) keeps you in context while linked to the big screen.
avoid: Five-step same-network Wi-Fi or Bluetooth discovery (screens 1 to 5) is slow and brittle compared with a QR on the debrief display for faculty pairing.
mobbin:f4a1c6f0-b7ae-427b-a896-b4f3c2535.fit: Mobile and iPad app: this is an example of what not to do for debrief pairing. Multi-step nearby discovery does not beat a QR-linked web page on the phone. Keep named-screen and Connected chrome if pairing is QR-first.

mobbin:3f1ac467-e548-499a-91bf-cd1e5a74a.summary: While browsing a title with Living Room TV already connected, the user opens the full remote and gets touchpad nav plus play/pause, seek, and ±30s skips for the big screen.
steps: Title detail with Connected bar and pause
steal: A docked bar naming Living Room TV with pause while browsing (screen 1) lets you control without leaving context.
A Connected header on the remote panel (screen 2) always shows which screen is driven.
±30s skips beside the scrubber (screen 2) support coarse jumps for debrief moments without precise scrubbing.
Large mute and volume targets under the touchpad (screen 2) are one-hand, glanceable audio and video controls.
avoid: A full swipe-to-navigate touchpad as primary (screen 2) is wrong for debrief. Debrief needs timeline and bookmarks, not TV focus navigation.
mobbin:3f1ac467-e548-499a-91bf-cd1e5a74a.fit: Mobile and iPad app: the phone beats desktop for faculty standing in the room driving the debrief big screen. Prefer a web remote with named screen and transport or skip after QR pair. That extends baseline private annotations and screen control.
